question: Is artificial general intelligence achievable within 20 years?

Research Question: Can an artificial intelligence system independently achieve human-level performance across a comprehensive set of cognitive tasks, including language understanding, problem-solving, and emotional intelligence, within the next 20 years?

To falsify this prediction, one would need to develop a rigorous benchmarking framework that encompasses a wide array of cognitive tasks representative of general human intelligence. If, after 20 years, no AI system can meet or exceed the established benchmarks across all these tasks, the prediction would be considered falsified.
Research Question: Will an artificial intelligence system, within the next 20 years, independently demonstrate human-level emotional intelligence across diverse real-world scenarios?

What is the evidence that AI systems will succeed in demonstrating genuine emotional understanding in open-ended, cross-cultural real-world scenarios through advanced modeling of human emotions and interactive learning?
